message.reasoning_content:
Analyze the kernel: notable risks — non-interleaved path handles odd headdim? Also cos/sin contiguity assumed (indexed as rm*rotary_dim_half, assumes cos contiguous). Interleaved path: cos indexing uses rk_half vs x loaded with rk full range — cos broadcast: cos shape [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K//2], x0 has shape [BLOCK_H, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K//2] after split. Broadcast of cos [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K//2] against [1, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K//2] fine. Non-interleaved: cos shape [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K//2] vs x0 [BLOCK_H, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K//2] — broadcast works.

Potential bug: cos/sin strides not passed — assumes cos is contiguous (seqlen, headdim/2). If headdim is odd? headdim//2. Also non-interleaved path assumes rotary_dim == headdim (full rotation), not partial rotary dim. Also grid = (nheads, seqlen) with BLOCK_H=1, BLOCK_M=1 fine.

Big suspect: non-interleaved formula sign: o0 = x0*cos - x1*sin, o1 = x0*sin + x1*cos — standard RoPE.

Interleaved path mask covers rk < 2*rotary_dim_half; if headdim odd, headdim//2*2 != headdim, last column untouched (out = empty_like, uninitialized garbage). Similarly non-interleaved only touches dim < headdim//2 and pair. Odd headdim unlikely.

Another risk: cos/sin indexed with rk_half < rotary_dim_half but block dim BLOCK_K//2 = next_pow2(headdim)/2 >= headdim/2, fine.

Interleaved reshape: x of shape [BLOCK_H, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K] reshaped to [..., BLOCK_K//2, 2] then split → x0 = even indices (2i), x1 = odd. Correct for interleaved pairing. tl.split requires last dim 2 — ok.
